q: Do pollution control systems like ESPs and bag filters add to my emissions?
title: ESPs and bag filters: electricity
short: Yes, through electricity: fans, ESP power supplies and compressed air for bag cleaning are Scope 2. You cannot switch them off, but you can cut their kWh with fan drives, cleaning on pressure drop and fixing air leaks. Sub-meter them to see their share.
audience: Cement, steel, boiler and foundry operators

ul: Induced draft fans pushing gas through the filter.
Compressed air pulses that clean filter bags.
Pulse cleaning triggered by pressure drop, not a timer.
Sealing duct leaks so fans move less air.

p: Never trade emission limits for energy. Agree changes with the pollution control board consent conditions.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.

sources.label: CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector
